IUCN Red List of Ecosystems

Global Red List of Coral Reef Ecosystems

What do criteria A–E mean?
A
Reduction in distribution: loss of functioning reef, measured as sites where coral cover fell below 5–10% (A1 past 50 years; A2 projected, next 50 years, Australia only)
B
Restricted distribution: very small or few reef areas, with ongoing threats
C
Abiotic degradation: more frequent marine heatwaves causing severe bleaching and mortality (C1 past 50 years; C2 projected heat stress, next 50 years, IPCC SSP2-4.5)
D
Biotic disruption: balance of corals, algae and fish (coral cover, algae-to-coral ratio, herbivorous and predatory fish)
E
Quantitative risk analysis: collapse modelling to 2075 (Great Barrier Reef and Torres Strait only)

The overall risk status is the highest category across all criteria. Collapse = near or complete loss of hard corals (below 5% cover).

Shown for visualization only, generalized to a ~1 km grid; not for download or redistribution. Ecoregions: IUCN Red List of Ecosystems (2026), based on the Marine Ecoregions of the World (Spalding et al. 2007).
